toFix.title: An empty POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT crashes the CLI instead of using the default
toFix.failureScenario: cli.env (or the environment) has `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=`, i.e. the commented example line uncommented but left blank. The cli.env loop stores "" in the map, so `env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse ...` gets "" and never builds the account URL. Every check passes, then `client.dict` -> `r2.Client.call` runs `c.endpoint[std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").? + 3 ..]` (src/r2.zig:84) on "". The find returns null, so the process panics (or hits UB in ReleaseFast) instead of printing one line and exiting 1. docs/specification.md:509 says "An empty value counts as missing", so the documented outcome is the default `https://<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`. `POSTILLA_DICT_DIR=` on line 186 has the same gap: it passes "" to `r2.dict`, and the command fails with `dict: FileNotFound` instead of using `./dict`.
toFix.evidence: src/cli.zig:68 `.endpoint = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse try std.fmt.allocPrint(a, "https://{s}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com", ...)`; src/r2.zig:84 `c.endpoint[std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").? + 3 ..]`; docs/specification.md:509 "An empty value counts as missing."
toFix.fix: Treat an empty value as unset at both reads, e.g. `const endpoint = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse "";` then `.endpoint = if (endpoint.len > 0) endpoint else try std.fmt.allocPrint(...)`. Do the same for POSTILLA_DICT_DIR, falling back to "./dict".
toFix.reason: The defect holds up against the code. In src/cli.zig:59 the cli.env loop stores any `KEY=` line with an empty value, and an empty value in the process env also lands in the map. The required-variable check at line 65 covers only the 8 required names. Line 68 uses `env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse ...`, so it falls back only when the key is absent, not when it is empty. With `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=` the endpoint is "". After all story.json and server-list checks pass, line 186 calls client.dict, which calls get and then r2.Client.call. src/r2.zig:84 does `std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").?` on "", which unwraps null: a panic in safe builds, UB in ReleaseFast. Nothing upstream stops it. The tests always set a non-empty endpoint (test/cli_publish.zig:200) and never try an empty one. This feature adds the rule "An empty value counts as missing" (docs/specification.md:509) and the commented `# POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=` line in cli.env.example, so the documented behaviour is the account default. The POSTILLA_DICT_DIR part is also real, but milder: an empty value gives a clean `dict: FileNotFound` and exit 1 instead of using ./dict, which breaks the spec but does not crash. Rating: rare, because the user has to uncomment the example line and leave it blank. Critical, because the process panics. Not silent, because it aborts loudly. The smallest fix is to treat empty as unset for both values, e.g. `const ep = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse "";` then `if (ep.len > 0) ep else allocPrint(...)`, and the same for the dict dir: about 3 added lines.
toFix.reproReason:
The bug is confirmed through a path a real user can reach. In /home/arrow/Development/postilla-backend/test/cli-publish_repro_r1_1.zig, a cli.env in the command's current directory contains the line `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=`, as when the example line is uncommented and left blank. The environment does not set the endpoint. The test then runs `cli.run(... "publish" <folder>)` against the real server (harness) with a story that passes every check. The test expects exit code 1 and an empty feed, because the empty endpoint should count as missing and the default should be used. Instead the test binary aborts with SIGABRT: "panic: attempt to use null value" at src/r2.zig:84:76 (`c.endpoint[std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").? + 3 ..]`). The stack runs through r2.Client.get, then r2.Client.dict, then src/cli.zig:186 in publish, then cli.run. This is exactly the failure the finding claims.

The account id in the test is `[`. With it, the default URL `https://[.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` is rejected at once by std.Uri.parse (InvalidFormat). So once the bug is fixed, the test passes quickly: one 'dict: ...' line, exit 1, no network calls and no retries.

I did not reproduce the second gap in the finding, `POSTILLA_DICT_DIR=`. Its default `./dict` is resolved against the process cwd (r2.dict uses Io.Dir.cwd()), not the cwd passed to cli.run. During `zig build test` that is the repo root, which has no `dict/`. A test that passes after a fix would need to create `<repo>/dict` or chdir, and chdir would break the harness's relative database path. The endpoint crash is the critical part, and it is confirmed. No production code was changed.

toFix.title: First publish fails with dict: FileNotFound when the dict cache directory doesn't exist
toFix.failureScenario: A fresh setup with the default `POSTILLA_DICT_DIR=./dict`: git can't track an empty directory, so nothing creates `./dict`. `postilla publish <folder>` passes story.json and the server-list checks, then calls `client.dict(io, a, "./dict")`. `r2.dict` immediately does `Io.Dir.cwd().openDir(io, dir_path, .{ .iterate = true })` (src/r2.zig:45). The directory is missing, so this returns FileNotFound, and the command exits 1 with `dict: FileNotFound`. It never downloads the build that docs/specification.md:417 says it downloads into POSTILLA_DICT_DIR "if it doesn't have it". The AC-9 test hides this because it creates the directory before running (test/cli_publish.zig:192 `createDirPath(io, "dict")`). r2.dict is pre-existing, but this diff adds its first caller and leans on it for the empty-cache case.
toFix.evidence: src/cli.zig:186 `client.dict(io, a, env.get("POSTILLA_DICT_DIR") orelse "./dict") catch |err| return fail(w, "dict: {t}", .{err})`; src/r2.zig:45 `var dir = try Io.Dir.cwd().openDir(io, dir_path, .{ .iterate = true });`; test/cli_publish.zig:192 `try w.tmp.dir.createDirPath(io, "dict");`
toFix.fix: Before `client.dict`, create the directory: `cwd.createDirPath(io, dict_dir) catch |err| return fail(w, "dict: {t}", .{err});`. Then drop the `createDirPath("dict")` from the test setup so AC-9 covers a cache directory that doesn't exist yet.
toFix.reason: The claim holds. r2.dict (src/r2.zig:45) calls `Io.Dir.cwd().openDir(io, dir_path, .{ .iterate = true })` with no create step, so a missing POSTILLA_DICT_DIR gives error.FileNotFound before anything is downloaded. Nothing upstream creates the directory: src/cli.zig:186 is the only caller of client.dict, and .gitignore, the repo and the docs have no mkdir or tracked dict/ folder. cli.env.example and specification.md:522 both default it to ./dict. The AC-9 fixture hides the bug by calling `createDirPath(io, "dict")` at test/cli_publish.zig:192, so no test covers a missing directory. As a result, the first `postilla publish` on a fresh checkout exits 1 with `dict: FileNotFound`, against spec line 417 ("downloads that build into POSTILLA_DICT_DIR if it doesn't have it") and against AC-9's empty-cache first publish. A base check could not reproduce it, because the publish command did not exist on the base, so it counts as feature-caused. Rating: common, since every fresh setup with the default hits it on the first publish. Major, since the command visibly fails on the normal path and breaks the intent of AC-9. Not silent, since it exits 1 with a message and the user can work around it by creating the directory. Smallest fix: in r2.dict, open the directory with a create-path variant (for example `createDirPathOpen`) instead of `openDir`, about 1 changed line.
toFix.reproReason: I wrote one integration test and it fails for the reason the finding gives. It runs `cli.run` with `postilla publish <folder>` against the real server (harness) and a bare local fake R2 that serves `dict/latest` and the fixture `dict.db.gz` and stores uploads. The story passes every check, and `POSTILLA_DICT_DIR` points at `<tmp>/dict`, which doesn't exist, as on a fresh setup. The command printed `dict: FileNotFound`: `r2.dict` opens the cache directory at src/r2.zig:45 without creating it, and the error comes out through src/cli.zig:186. So the first publish never downloads the build into `POSTILLA_DICT_DIR`, which docs/specification.md:417 says it does. As a control, I created `dict/` in the same test and reran it: it passed (exit 0, build cached, story in the feed). The only thing behind the failure is the missing directory. I did not touch production code.

toFix.title: Empty or scheme-less POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT crashes publish instead of failing with a message
toFix.failureScenario: A cli.env has the line `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=`. That is the example's commented line uncommented with no value, the same as every other `KEY=` line in cli.env.example. A value with no scheme, such as `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=acct.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, does the same. `env.get` returns "" (or the bare host), not null, so the `orelse` default is skipped. All checks and list GETs pass. Then `client.dict` -> `get("dict/latest")` -> `call` runs `std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").?` on a null result. In Debug and ReleaseSafe the process panics with 'attempt to use null value'. In ReleaseFast the endpoint is sliced out of bounds (UB). Either way it does not exit 1 with one line naming the variable. That breaks the spec's rule that a failing command prints one line naming the step and exits non-zero, and the doc line added by this diff ('An empty value counts as missing'), which this optional variable does not follow. Before the diff the endpoint was always built as `https://<account>...`, so the unwrap could not be reached. The new env variable exposes it.
toFix.evidence: src/cli.zig:68 `.endpoint = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse try std.fmt.allocPrint(a, "https://{s}.r2.cloudflarestorage.com", ...)`; src/r2.zig:84 `c.endpoint[std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").? + 3 ..]`; docs/specification.md (CLI config, added in this diff): "An empty value counts as missing."; cli.env.example:26 `# POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=`
toFix.fix: In publish, use the default when the value is missing or empty: `const endpoint = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse "";` then `if (endpoint.len == 0)` fall back to the account URL. Refuse a value with no `://` with `return fail(w, "POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT: not a URL", .{});` before the first R2 call.
toFix.reason:
The reported defect is real. The cli.env loader at src/cli.zig:55-62 stores `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=` as an empty string, so `env.get` returns "" and not null. The required-variable loop only checks the 8 required names, so it skips this one. At line 68 the `orelse` then keeps "" (or a host with no scheme) as `client.endpoint`. Every R2 call goes through r2.Client.call (src/r2.zig), which runs `std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").?`. On a null result that panics in safe builds and is UB in ReleaseFast. It is never turned into a one-line error with exit 1.

This breaks two things in the spec: the CLI-config rule "An empty value counts as missing", where a missing value should fall back to the default `https://<account>...`, and the rule that a failing command prints one line and exits non-zero. The feature causes it: the base build always made the endpoint with `https://`, and POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT, the cli.env.example line and the doc row are all new in this diff. No test covers it. The only test sets a valid endpoint (test/cli_publish.zig:200).

Rating:
- Chance is rare. The variable ships commented out, so a user has to uncomment it and leave it empty, or type a host without a scheme.
- It is a crash, which the table rates critical. It happens before any upload, so no data is lost.
- It is not silent: the process aborts with a panic.
- The smallest fix treats an empty value as unset, for example `const ep = env.get("POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT") orelse ""; .endpoint = if (ep.len > 0) ep else try allocPrint(...)`. Also failing with a message when the value has no "://" adds about 1-2 more lines.
toFix.reproReason: The finding is confirmed for the scheme-less case. The test calls the public `cli.run` against the real server harness. Its `cli.env` holds `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=acct.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` and the story passes every check. Run with `zig build test -Dtest-file=test/cli-publish_repro_r1_3.zig`, it crashes with SIGABRT before it can exit 1: "panic: attempt to use null value" at src/r2.zig:84:76, on `c.endpoint[std.mem.find(u8, c.endpoint, "://").? + 3 ..]`. The path to the panic is r2.Client.call <- get("dict/latest") <- dict <- cli.zig:186 publish <- cli.run. This new file does not cover the empty `POSTILLA_R2_ENDPOINT=` case, because test/cli-publish_repro_r1_1.zig already reproduces it on the same path. No production code was changed.
